_citation: Hall, M. & Geissler, A. (FHNW), 'Thermal comfort in Passive Solar Houses in Ladakh (Simulation of HIAL's PSH, wp 2.2)', v6.0, 2022-01-26. Funded by Swiss FDFA/SDC. Project partners: HIAL (Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Leh), TERI, FHNW.
_use: Ground-truth reference for Phase 2 solver validation. Two independent checks: (1) steady-state U-value of their PreFreb wall/roof assembly, reproduced with our ConstructionAssembly and compared to their published U-values; (2) transient sanity check using their Leh TMY monthly-mean temperatures as forcing.

leh_tmy_monthly_mean_temp_c._source: NREL Leh TMY dataset (34941_34.15_77.55_tmy.csv), as tabulated in the FHNW report Table 8

ground_temp_monthly_c._source: FHNW report Table 8, derived per EN ISO 13370 from Leh TMY data

prefreb_wall_construction.note: report lists this as '25cm straw-clay/reinforced concrete + 10cm insulation'; we use plain strawclay_block (no rebar) since the RC contribution is small-area (every third cavity) and not separately quantified

prefreb_roof_construction.note: report's actual roof stack (waterproofing/mud plaster/20cm strawclay/plywood/20cm pashmina wool/plywood) is more complex than our materials library can fully reproduce (no pashmina-wool entry); this is a simplified single-dominant-layer check, expect our U-value to differ from theirs more than the wall check does

measurement_vs_simulation_benchmark._source: FHNW report Table 12 (best-tuned model, 07.01-12.02.2021, west room)
measurement_vs_simulation_benchmark.note: this is THEIR simulation-vs-measurement error, not a target for us to beat -- it's the benchmark for what good agreement looks like in this exact climate/building type. Use it to judge whether our RMSE/MAE (once we have real measured or high-confidence comparison data) is in a reasonable range.
